newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lamfalussy-current EU exch rates seem sustainable.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy-current EU exch rates seem sustainable.

text.p: European Monetary Institute president Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Tuesday that there are early indications that current exchange rate levels among European Union countries are sustainable.
In a speech in Lisbon marking the anniversary of the Banco de Portugal, Lamfalussy said "there are also tentative indications that current exchange rate levels are sustainable."
The EMI made a copy of the speech available in Frankfurt.
"Evidence regarding current real exchange rates does not suggest misalignments in the ERM which could by themselves trigger major corrective forces," he said.
But he added that caution was warranted regarding exchange rate predictions because of possible external turbulence such as swings in the U.S. dollar.
Lamfalussy said a majority within the EMI council believe a currency should belong to the Exchange Rate Mechanism before joining monetary union.
